programs.title: World's Most Scenic Railway Journeys
programs.desc: BAFTA-winning actor Bill Nighy, known for, among others,from the film "Love Actually", invites viewers to another series of railway journeys through picturesque corners of the world.The New Zealand route starts in Greymouth and goes through Arthur's Pass National Park, Cass, the Waimakiriri Gorge and Christchurch.Bill also discovers the charms of Taiwan and Norwegian landscapes from the train windows on the distance from Bergen to Oslo.Viewers will also take an exciting trip on the Austrian Transalpine Railway, which crosses the snow-capped peaks of Tyrol.

programs.title: Solar System
programs.desc: The host of the program, Professor Brian Cox, presents selected information about the solar system.Viewers will learn about planets and moons covered with volcanoes that erupt with fire and ice.In the following parts, the scientist talks about the most interesting atmospheric conditions that were noticed on celestial bodies neighboring the Earth.He visits landscapes created by dust whirls, mountains covered with metallic frost and monsoon rains on one of the moons.Additionally, Professor Cox will introduce viewers to frozen regions of the solar system, including a dwarf planet with mountains of solid ice floating on it, as well as a black and white moon.

Joanna Lumley's Spice Trail Adventure
programs.desc: Actress Joanna Lumley, known from the films "Absolutely Fabulous" and "The Wolf of Wall Street", goes on an expedition to discover the origins of spices.It follows two continents in the footsteps of pharaohs, crusaders and rulers.He visits the Indonesian Banda Islands, which were once the only place on Earth where nutmeg grew.He also visits Madagascar, the place of the largest vanilla cultivation.It also goes to India and the Middle East.He realizes that for hundreds of years, the East and the West have been linked by the spice trade.

programs.title: Gordon Buchanan: My Epic Camel Adventure
programs.desc: Scottish filmmaker and TV presenter Gordon Buchanan begins his expedition through the Gobi Desert.He decides to do it on a camel, a traditional Mongolian means of transport.An animal adapted to living in a dry and hot climate will help it survive in the wilderness, rocky plains, desert dunes and the dangerous Bumbat Mountain.Gordon wants to get to know his animal companions better.It provides them with food and benefits from the warmth of their fur.He also benefits from the hospitality of nomads who live a wandering lifestyle.The journey helps him understand that climate change has direct consequences not only for animals, but also for people who inhabit the vast steppes.
